articles.title: Enhancing unsupervised learning with correlation-based 𝑘 -medoids: A case study on citrus price dynamics
articles.abstract: In this study, we propose a clustering approach based on 𝑘 -medoids to detect price trend patterns of citrus products based on their prices at origin (2015-2024) in the Comunitat Valenciana (Spain). Each variety is treated as an independent observation for each combination of year and province, calculating different characteristics, including duration, variability, and linear regression parameters. The novelty lies in coupling correlation dissimilarities with 𝑘 -medoid representatives and an assignment of five characteristics that preserves the structure while improving interpretability. This approach reveals a stable structure of three clusters of price variation (down, flat, up). Robustness is supported by subsample consensus (Proportion of Ambiguous Clustering, PAC, attains its minimum at 𝑘 = 3 ) and by internal indices; external validation shows a moderate but significant agreement with an independent indicator derived from official weekly reports (e.g., season-level Accuracy 0.52 or permutation 𝑝 = 0 . 0 0 1 ). Finally, clusters relate to economic drivers: variety group shows a moderate association, province a weak one, and continuous drivers (as duration or price variance) differ across clusters as expected. Altogether, the approach offers a reproducible tool to monitor citrus price evolution and their variations from one season to another.

articles.title: The normalized difference layer: A differentiable spectral index formulation for deep learning
articles.abstract: Normalized difference indices have been a staple in remote sensing for decades. They stay reliable under lighting changes produce bounded values and connect well to biophysical signals. Even so, they are usually treated as a fixed pre processing step with coefficients set to one, which limits how well they can adapt to a specific learning task. In this study, we introduce the Normalized Difference Layer that is a differentiable neural network module. The proposed method keeps the classical idea but learns the band coefficients from data. We present a complete mathematical framework for integrating this layer into deep learning architectures that uses softplus reparameterization to ensure positive coefficients and bounded denominators. We describe forward and backward pass algorithms enabling end to end training through backpropagation. This approach preserves the key benefits of normalized differences, namely illumination invariance and outputs bounded to $[-1,1]$ while allowing gradient descent to discover task specific band weightings. We extend the method to work with signed inputs, so the layer can be stacked inside larger architectures. Experiments show that models using this layer reach similar classification accuracy to standard multilayer perceptrons while using about 75\% fewer parameters. They also handle multiplicative noise well, at 10\% noise accuracy drops only 0.17\% versus 3.03\% for baseline MLPs. The learned coefficient patterns stay consistent across different depths.

articles.title: Application of the W-shaped process for a Reinforcement Learning use case on drone navigation
articles.abstract: The interest in Machine Learning (ML) has spread to safety systems due to its ability to solve tasks that cannot be explicitly programmed, including pattern recognition, object detection, and autonomous control. To ensure the safe integration of ML in avionics, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) proposed the W-shaped development process. However, it focuses on supervised learning, leaving aside Reinforcement Learning (RL), which is particularly suitable for decision-making problems. This paper presents a practical analysis of the applicability of the W-shaped process to systems that include RL components. To support this analysis, the W-shaped process is applied to a drone navigation and collision avoidance system under safety requirements on a real-time embedded platform. This paper demonstrates that processes related to learning must be adapted to support the interactive nature of RL, while those related to implementation are agnostic to the ML technique and thus compatible with RL. This paper also proposes concrete adaptations, including scenario-based data management, a reinterpretation of data quality requirements, and the explicit definition of the agent-environment interface before training.

articles.title: FuseDepth: Zero-shot metric depth with semantic–geometric fusion of foundation visual priors
articles.abstract: Recent monocular depth estimators show strong zero-shot generalization, but many remain unreliable under strict metric evaluation: relative-depth foundation models often need test-time scale/shift alignment, while metric predictors can suffer scale drift and blurred depth discontinuities under domain shift. We present FuseDepth, a prior-guided framework for zero-shot metric monocular depth estimation that injects boundary and geometric cues into a frozen foundation-depth backbone. FuseDepth adapts Depth Anything v2 with lightweight LoRA modules and a boundary-regularized local metric-scale field to obtain a coarse metric prediction. It then refines this prediction using a matting-derived surface-interaction graph whose nodes represent detected surface hypotheses and whose edges encode overlap, boundary adjacency, and contour proximity to define a soft occlusion jump set. Refinement is controlled by a learned prior-reliability gate that arbitrates between metric scale, contour evidence, and monocular surface-normal priors, rather than simply concatenating external features. We evaluate FuseDepth on unseen SYNS, DDAD, and DIODE benchmarks against relative and metric baselines under a strict target-domain zero-shot protocol with no target calibration. Across datasets, FuseDepth improves AbsRel and SILog and reduces per-image log-scale bias. Boundary-specific evaluation now covers SYNS, DDAD, and both DIODE splits, where FuseDepth consistently improves RGB-edge alignment and depth-edge F1 while DepthPro retains a small DBE or precision advantage on some splits. A target-affine oracle sensitivity analysis shows that DAv2 and Marigold improve when target ground truth is allowed for calibration, yet FuseDepth without target calibration retains lower AbsRel and SILog and higher δ 1 on every evaluated target. On DDAD, the gain is reproduced across three independently trained seeds and across all three geographic subsets. Mechanism-isolation, natural-prior-quality, wrong-prior, graph-sensitivity, and deployment-resource analyses further characterize when the structured prior fusion helps and what computational cost it incurs.

articles.title: Physics-informed neural networks for the fractional Fokker–Planck equation in a Heston-type stochastic volatility model with time-dependent parameters
articles.abstract: This work presents a physics-informed neural network framework for solving the time-fractional Fokker–Planck equation governing the joint probability density of asset price and stochastic volatility in a Heston-type model with fully time-dependent parameters. Memory effects are incorporated through a Caputo fractional derivative of order α = 2 H ∈ ( 0,1 ) , where the Hurst exponent H ∈ ( 0 , 1 2 ] characterizes anomalous subdiffusion, and the formulation naturally recovers the classical Heston Fokker–Planck equation when H = 1 2 . The governing equation is embedded directly into the neural network loss function alongside initial, boundary, and normalization constraints, yielding a mesh-free solver that handles strongly coupled time-dependent coefficients without grid construction. The principal finding is that time-dependent parameters substantially amplify the non-Gaussian character of the stochastic volatility process, producing broader probability distributions with higher kurtosis and stronger volatility clustering within the truncated computational domain than those obtained using constant-parameter fractional models. Comparisons with finite difference, spectral, and Monte Carlo methods confirm the accuracy and robustness of the proposed approach. Applied to European option pricing, the framework generates realistic implied volatility skews and option prices that systematically exceed Black–Scholes benchmarks, particularly for out-of-the-money contracts, demonstrating the practical importance of combining fractional memory with time-varying stochastic volatility in financial modeling.

articles.title: Adapting reinforcement learning with chain-of-thought supervision for explainable detection of hateful and propagandistic memes
articles.abstract: Hateful and propagandistic memes exploit the interplay between images and text to convey harmful intent that neither modality reveals alone. Although thinking-based multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have advanced vision-language understanding, their application to meme content moderation remains underexplored. We propose a reinforcement learning-based post-training method that improves classification performance and reference-based explanation quality in thinking-based MLLMs via task-specific rewards and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Concretely, we (i) conduct a systematic empirical study of off-the-shelf MLLMs for hateful and propagandistic meme understanding across English and Arabic benchmarks, (ii) extend existing meme datasets with weakly supervised chain-of-thought (CoT) rationales via distillation and multi-LLM fine-grained propaganda annotations, (iii) introduce a GRPO-based objective with thinking-length regularization that jointly optimizes classification accuracy and explanation quality, and (iv) investigate self-supervised GRPO on unlabeled memes using consensus-based pseudo-labels. Experiments on the Hateful Memes and ArMeme benchmarks show that our approach improves over previously reported results on FHM accuracy (up to +2.1%, from 79.9% to 82.0%) and on ArMeme macro-F1 (up to +7.6 points, from 0.536 to 0.612 with explanations; +6.1 compared to the original ArMeme benchmark), while also generating natural-language explanations. On ArMeme, sequence-classification baselines remain stronger in terms of raw accuracy, whereas our approach provides more balanced per-class performance along with explanations. We publicly release our code, data extensions, and evaluation resources.

articles.title: Conceptualizing automated surface quality: A cross-domain evidence synthesis from CNNs to transformers
articles.abstract: ABSTRACT The automation of surface defect detection is undergoing a paradigm shift from CNN-based to Transformer and hybrid architectures. Yet, the field lacks a structured synthesis connecting this architectural evolution to industrial grade-readiness, the capacity of a detection system to translate its outputs into actionable quality classifications. This PICOS-ES-guided systematic review addresses that gap by synthesizing 55 peer-reviewed studies (2015-2025) across textile, steel, wood, ceramic, and electronics manufacturing, extending the conventional PICOS framework with Evidence Source as a sixth dimension to enable systematic assessment of dataset reproducibility. Using a dual-assessment protocol (12-item quality appraisal and 6-domain risk-of-bias evaluation via QUADAS-2 and APPRAISE-AI), the review reports benchmark performance exceeding 0.84 mAP/F1 across the corpus, with hierarchical clustering identifying three study-quality profiles: high-quality low-bias (78.2%), high-quality with reproducibility concerns (14.5%), and moderate-quality (7.3%). Domain analysis reveals steel (37.5%) and textile (17.9%) dominance and an architectural transition from CNN-dominant (2015-2021) to Transformer-hybrid (2024-2025) approaches. Despite these advances, persistent bottlenecks remain: limited cross-domain generalizability, reporting heterogeneity (60.7% of studies omit computational-efficiency metrics), and a critical underutilization of grade-readiness capabilities linking detection to industrial quality standards. These findings motivate a call for standardized, transparent reporting, mandatory code/data sharing, and future research that integrates detection, grading, and actionable decision-making to move surface defect analytics from technical demonstration to validated industrial deployment.

articles.title: A hybrid quantitative–qualitative RAG approach for territorial well-being decision support
articles.abstract: Territorial well-being analysis requires integrating two complementary families of information: objective indicators (equipment, composite quality-of-life scores) that characterize structural conditions, and subjective perceptions (citizen survey verbatims, interviews) that reflect lived experience. Classical retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) handles such mixed-source queries poorly: semantic similarity search fragments information and provides no structural constraint on the consistency between the data types a query calls for and those actually available. We propose a hybrid RAG architecture built on three principles: (i) explicit decomposition of the user query into independently processed sub-questions; (ii) multi-level synthetic representations precomputed along business-driven analytical views, adapting the RAPTOR approach to survey metadata rather than automatic clustering; and (iii) a typed decomposition mechanism enforcing consistency between the nature of the query and the sub-questions generated, constraining the formulation of sub-questions that have no documentary support. We evaluate the architecture on a benchmark of 109 manually designed questions spanning seven usage categories, combining categorical retrieval metrics with a multi-dimensional LLM-as-judge validated against human annotations, an ablation study isolating each principle, and a comparison with an external decomposition baseline (Self-Ask). Results show that the architecture retrieves relevant sources far more exhaustively than vanilla RAG (Recall 0.97 against 0.68), that both the typing rule and the multi-level representations contribute significantly to answer quality, and that it outperforms Self-Ask. On the benchmark as a whole, answer quality is comparable to vanilla RAG, the advantage being concentrated on questions requiring multi-aspect reasoning—which suggests that architectural choices should be informed by the intended usage profile.
